subject: Conversation slowpath: observed elevated streaming latency and short-term fixes
messages:
From: Emily Soto <emily@atlashealth.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: AtlasHealth Support <support@atlashealth.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production — intermittent long tail on chat streaming (started 09:00 PDT)

Vivek —

We're seeing repeated long tails on streaming responses from the chat endpoint starting around 09:00 PDT. Typical user session: initial token stream arrives, then a 3–8s stall before the rest of the tokens arrive. This is impacting our support chat SLA and causing a lot of dropped sessions.

We captured a few session IDs and attached a small telemetry bundle. Can you confirm whether this is something on your side or if we should look at client-side timeouts?

Example session IDs: s-9a3f, s-9a4b
Impact: ~15% of chats in US-west intermittently affected, higher during our morning peak.

Thanks,
Emily Soto
Product Manager — AtlasHealth

--

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>

Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 09:34:40 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production — intermittent long tail on chat streaming (started 09:00 PDT)

Emily — thanks for pinging and for the telemetry. We're seeing the same signal in our edge metrics (US-west edge shard #7) and are triaging now. Short answer: this looks like a short-lived slowpath where the runtime is emitting the first chunk, then hitting an internal batching window under a particular token cadence which produces a 2–8s gap.

Immediate next steps (what I'll do now):
- Ask engineering to push a targeted hotfix that reduces the batching window on the affected edge shard and forces immediate KV-cache warm paths for pinned sessions.
- Provide you with two temporary client-side mitigations you can enable quickly: 1) extend your client-side streaming receive timeout to 10s; 2) enable a small automatic fallback to non-streaming completion for sessions that see no token for >3s (we'll give sample code).
- Share a short list of configuration changes (we'll include a patch you can apply if desired).

I've looped in Karthik (runtime) and Laura (CS lead) to coordinate. Expect another update in ~45–60 minutes.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference

--

From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Emily Soto <emily@atlashealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 10:05:12 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production — intermittent long tail on chat streaming (started 09:00 PDT)

Following up with the engineering findings from the triage:

Root cause (preliminary): a regression in an optimization that attempted to increase token throughput by coalescing small requests into a slightly larger batch. Under a narrow cadence distribution (frequent short responses followed by brief silence) this caused the scheduler to defer the next dispatch while waiting for the batching window. The deferral shows up as the 2–8s gap you're seeing.

What we changed (actions completed at 09:50 PDT):
- Reduced the coalescing window for the affected shard from 60ms -> 8ms for low-latency tiers.
- Forced KV-cache pin for long-lived chat sessions from AtlasHealth (so lookups don't trigger an extra cold path).
- Deployed an emergency kernel pin that prefers the low-latency exec path for short-sequence completions.

Customer-visible mitigation we recommend immediately:
1) Increase client streaming receive timeout to 10s; sample: if no bytes for 3s then keep connection open but mark as backoff and wait up to 10s before fallback.
2) Add a lightweight client fallback: if you receive the initial token and no progress for 3s, call /v1/completions (non-streaming) as a retry path.
3) Toggle on our suggested session pinning flag (see hotfix-config.patch) if you want us to apply the same behavior server-side for your org only.

We're keeping the change in canary for the shard and will roll to prod after 1 hour of clean telemetry. I'll keep you updated.

-Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
From: Emily Soto <emily@atlashealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 11:20:05 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production — intermittent long tail on chat streaming (started 09:00 PDT)

Thanks — the mitigations helped immediately. We've enabled the client-side fallback and extended receive timeouts; the error rate dropped and user-reported drops decreased. Appreciate the quick canary.

Two asks for follow-up:
1) Can you confirm whether this qualifies for an operational credit under our SLA (we hit degradation during peak hours)?
2) We'd like a short postmortem and a timeline of the changes so we can present to our ops leadership tomorrow.

Emily
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Soto <emily@atlashealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 3 Oct 2026 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Post-incident summary — AtlasHealth streaming slowpath (01 Oct 2026)

Emily —

Thanks again for the fast signal and for applying the temporary client mitigations. Below is the post-incident summary and next steps; we'll provide a formal PDF you can share with leadership by Monday.

Summary:
- Window: 2026-10-01 09:00–10:05 PDT (impact concentrated 09:00–09:50).
- Scope: ~15% of chat sessions routed through US-west shard #7 experienced intermittent 2–8s token delivery gaps; overall completion correctness unaffected.
- Root cause: an over-aggressive batching/coalescing regression in the serving runtime scheduler that increased dispatch latency in specific cadence distributions.

Remediation timeline:
- 09:18 PDT: AtlasHealth reported issue and provided telemetry.
- 09:34 PDT: Initial acknowledgement and immediate mitigations suggested (client timeouts + fallback).
- 09:50 PDT: Engineering deployed targeted canary: reduced batching window, KV-cache pin, kernel pin.
- 10:12 PDT: Canary telemetry clean; progressive rollout to remaining US-west capacity completed by 10:05 PDT.

Customer impact and credits:
- We're classifying this as a latency degradation incident. Marissa (cc'd) will coordinate a goodwill operational credit consistent with our SLA policy. Marissa, can you confirm the credit timeline and amount and loop finance if needed?

Permanent fixes and follow-ups:
- Revert the overly aggressive coalescing heuristic and add a deterministic guard for cadence distributions.
- Add an automatic sentinel that detects unusually long inter-token gaps and triggers routing to low-latency path without human intervention.
- Create a small evergreen doc for recommended client fallbacks (we'll share sample code and a small SDK helper to handle the fallback to non-streaming).
- Deliver a formal postmortem doc and link to the Jira ticket (INF-4721).

If you'd like a quick 20-min call to walk leadership through the timeline, Karthik and I are available Monday morning. Appreciate the partnership here — we'll follow up with the formal postmortem and the credit confirmation.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
